inventory.visualPurpose: Table 1 “Drug reactions—neurologic” (book 250): the seven neurologic adverse-reaction rows (cinchonism, Parkinson-like syndrome, peripheral neuropathy, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, seizures, tardive dyskinesia, visual disturbances) with their causal agents and notes
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-ph25/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): a three-column table (DRUG REACTION / CAUSAL AGENTS / NOTES) with seven rows in printed order — [1] Cinchonism: Quinidine, quinine; can present with tinnitus, hearing/vision loss, psychosis, and cognitive impairment; [2] Parkinson-like syndrome: Antipsychotics, metoclopramide; cogwheel rigidity of arm; [3] Peripheral neuropathy: Platinum agents (eg, cisplatin), isoniazid, vincristine, paclitaxel, phenytoin; “Cis, it’s very painful peripherally” (red mnemonic); [4] Idiopathic intracranial hypertension: Corticosteroids, danazol, vitamin A, growth hormones, tetracyclines; “Crime and debt Always grow head tension”; [5] Seizures: Isoniazid, bupropion, imipenem/cilastatin, tramadol; “With seizures, I bit my tongue”; [6] Tardive dyskinesia: Antipsychotics, metoclopramide; NOTES cell EMPTY; [7] Visual disturbances: Topiramate (blurred vision/diplopia, haloes), hydroxychloroquine (↓ visual acuity, visual field defects), digoxin (yellow-tinged vision), isoniazid (optic neuritis), ivabradine (luminous phenomena), PDE-5 inhibitors (blue-tinged vision), ethambutol (color vision changes), vigabatrin (tunnel vision); “These horrible drugs iirritate Precious eyes” (the source's own double-i print — two red mnemonic i's, one each for Isoniazid and Ivabradine). Drug-reaction names print teal (0x165d7e); mnemonic initial letters print red bold (0xb82837) in both causal-agent and notes cells.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual's Zone A (the nigrostriatal dopamine fork: shared culprits antipsychotics + metoclopramide → D2 blockade → acute down-state = Parkinson-like syndrome vs chronic up-regulation = tardive dyskinesia) + Zone B (the seven-row strip in printed order) + Zone C (the seizure-threshold gauge and the peripheral-axon panel with the INH-triple chip); the table's full text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's blocks[1], core.what, mechanisms, and recall

inventory.visualPurpose: Table 2 “Drug reactions—renal/genitourinary” (book 250): the four renal/GU adverse-reaction rows (Fanconi syndrome, hemorrhagic cystitis, interstitial nephritis, nephrotoxicity)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE, no raster (census as sv1): a three-column table with four rows in printed order — [1] Fanconi syndrome: Cisplatin, ifosfamide, expired tetracyclines, tenofovir (NOTES cell empty); [2] Hemorrhagic cystitis: Cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide; prevent by coadministering with mesna; [3] Interstitial nephritis: Diuretics (Pee), NSAIDs (Pain-free), Penicillins and cephalosporins, PPIs, rifamPin, sulfa drugs; “Remember the 5 P’s” — the causal-agents cell carries the IN-CELL 5-P mnemonic with red capital P's printed inside the words (raw-span confirmed: a red-bold P glyph sits inside “rifamPin”; a red “s” heads “sulfa”); [4] Nephrotoxicity: Cisplatin, aminoglycosides, amphotericin, vancomycin (NOTES cell empty). Teal reaction names; red mnemonic initials.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual's Zone D renal/genitourinary strip (the nephron-and-bladder descent: proximal tubule → bladder → interstitium → nephron at large, with the 5-P line, the in-cell rifamPin capital-P note, and the mesna chip); the table's full text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's blocks[2], core.what, mechanism 2, and recall

inventory.visualPurpose: Table 3 “Drug reactions—respiratory” (book 250): dry cough (ACE inhibitors) and pulmonary fibrosis (the six-drug row)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE, no raster (census as sv1): a three-column table with two rows in printed order — [1] Dry cough: ACE inhibitors (NOTES cell empty); [2] Pulmonary fibrosis: Methotrexate, nitrofurantoin, carmustine, bleomycin, busulfan, amiodarone (the causal-agents cell ends exactly “bleomycin, busulfan, amiodarone”); “My nose cannot breathe bad air” (red mnemonic initials M/n/c/b/b/a). TEXT-LAYER INTERLEAVE: the extracted NOTES column header prints AFTER both data rows (a documented cache-layer artifact; the printed grid is ordinary).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual's Zone D respiratory panel (bradykinin accumulation = dry cough vs alveolar scarring = the six-drug fibrosis row, with the mnemonic rendered red and the exact cell ending noted); the table's full text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's blocks[3] and recall

inventory.visualPurpose: Table 4 “Drug reactions—multiorgan” (book 250): antimuscarinic effects and the disulfiram-like reaction
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE, no raster (census as sv1): a three-column table with two rows in printed order — [1] Antimuscarinic: Atropine, TCAs, H1-blockers (printed with a subscript 1), antipsychotics (NOTES cell empty); [2] Disulfiram-like reaction: 1st-generation sulfonylureas, procarbazine, certain cephalosporins, griseofulvin, metronidazole; “Sorry pals, can’t go mingle” (red mnemonic initials s/p/c/g/m; VLM + raw-span confirmed as the DISULFIRAM row's NOTES cell — the red 'S' prints in the NOTES column on the same line as the causal agents). TEXT-LAYER INTERLEAVE: the footer slug and timestamp extract between the causal agents and the NOTES header + mnemonic (documented cache-layer artifact).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual's Zone D multiorgan panel (RECEPTOR BLOCK = muscarinic receptor vs ENZYME BLOCK = aldehyde dehydrogenase, with the mnemonic rendered red and the acetaldehyde note); the table's full text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's blocks[4] and recall
